question: A 73-year-old man comes to the physician because of worsening bilateral lower extremity pain for the past 8 months. The pain begins after walking one to two blocks and radiates bilaterally down the buttocks with cramping and tingling. He reports that the pain is worse while walking downhill and is relieved by sitting and leaning forward. He has hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He had a myocardial infarction at the age of 55 years and an abdominal aortic aneurysm repair at the age of 60 years. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years. He does not drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. His current medications include sitagliptin, metformin, atorvastatin, metoprolol succinate, amlodipine, and hydrochlorothiazide. His temperature is 37.5°C (99.5°F), pulse is 82/min, respirations are 17/min, and blood pressure is 150/87 mm Hg. Examination shows full muscle strength. Sensation is reduced bilaterally in the feet and toes. Straight leg raise is negative. X-ray of the spine shows degenerative changes. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

options.opb: Measurement of the ankle brachial index

paths: (Spinal stenosis of lumbar region)-CAUSES->(Low Back Pain)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(Degenerative abnormality)
(Spinal stenosis of lumbar region)-CAUSES->(Low Back Pain)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(Musculoskeletal torsion, function)-PROCESS_OF->(Pes)
(Spinal stenosis of lumbar region)-CAUSES->(Low Back Pain)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(Degenerative abnormality)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Lumbar spinal stenosis -> neurogenic claudication symptoms -> worsening bilateral lower extremity pain -> 80% CHAIN: Lumbar spinal stenosis -> degenerative changes on spine X-ray -> possible compression of nerve roots -> bilateral lower extremity pain -> 70% CHAIN: Lumbar spinal stenosis -> reduced sensation in feet and toes -> possible nerve compression -> bilateral lower extremity pain -> 80%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation of worsening bilateral lower extremity pain, especially with walking downhill and relief with sitting and leaning forward, along with reduced sensation in the feet and toes, suggests lumbar spinal stenosis. The most appropriate next step in diagnosis would be an MRI scan of the spine to confirm the presence of spinal stenosis and assess the extent of nerve compression.
analysis: The patient's clinical presentation, including worsening bilateral lower extremity pain exacerbated by walking downhill and relieved by sitting and leaning forward, along with reduced sensation in the feet and toes, strongly suggests lumbar spinal stenosis. Given the enhanced information provided, an MRI scan of the spine is the most appropriate next step to confirm the diagnosis and evaluate nerve compression.
